formulas.name: Carrier (pilot) protection
f: Power-line carrier (30–500 kHz) compares both line ends:
notes: Tip: Instant tripping for faults anywhere on the line (100% coverage).

formulas.name: Generator protection
f: Stator differential, restricted earth fault, negative sequence
(unbalance), loss of excitation, reverse power, over-speed,
notes: Tip: Reverse power relay protects the turbine when the generator motors.

formulas.name: Transformer protection
notes: Tip: 2nd-harmonic restraint prevents tripping on magnetising inrush.

formulas.name: Motor protection
f: Thermal overload, single phasing (negative sequence), short
circuit, earth fault, under-voltage, locked rotor
notes: Tip: Single phasing is the most common cause of motor burn-out.

formulas.name: Earthing
notes: Where: ρ = soil resistivity, l = rod length, d = diameter
Tip: Pipe/plate/rod earthing. Substations: < 1 Ω; large power stations < 0.5 Ω. Wenner 4-electrode method measures ρ.

formulas.name: Lightning protection
notes: Tip: Arrester discharge current and residual voltage must be below equipment BIL with margin.

formulas.name: DC distributor voltage drop
f: Fed at one end, concentrated loads : drop = Σ I<sub>section</sub>
uniformly loaded (i A/m, length l) : drop = irl 22
notes: Where: r = resistance per metre (both conductors)
Tip: Fed at both ends with equal voltage → drop reduced to ¼ of one-end feeding (uniform load).

formulas.name: AC distribution
f: Drop = I(R cos φ + X sin φ) per section (using each section's
notes: Where: I = section current, R, X = section resistance and reactance, φ = load pf angle
Tip: Radial, ring main, interconnected — reliability increases in that order.

formulas.name: Deregulation
f: Separation of generation, transmission and distribution
notes: Tip: Energy trading via day-ahead markets (IEX).

formulas.name: Energy conservation & audit
notes: Where: power in kW, hours per year; payback in years
Tip: Preliminary (walk-through) and detailed audits; Energy Conservation Act 2001; BEE star labels.

mcqs.q: Q1. A lightning arrester is connected
opts: (b) In the secondary of a CT
mcqs.ans: Ans: (d) Between line and earth It conducts the surge to earth and stops afterwards.

mcqs.q: Q2. Earth resistance of a large substation should be about
mcqs.ans: Ans: (a) ≤ 1 Ω Power stations ≈ 0.5 Ω, large substations ≈ 1 Ω.

opts: (d) High-frequency signals over the power line
mcqs.ans: Ans: (d) High-frequency signals over the power line (PLCC) Compares both ends of a long line.

mcqs.q: Q4. Uniformly loaded DC distributor fed at one end: total drop
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) i r L²/2 Fed at both ends with equal voltages: i r L²/8.
